opportunities.title: Prevention Planning Consultation Services
opportunities.description: The San Mateo County Human Services Agency (HSA), Children and Family Services (CFS) branch, is seeking proposals from qualified firms with demonstrated expertise in California child welfare systems, the Family First Prevention Services Act (FFPSA), Title IV-E Prevention Services, Community Pathways, fiscal claiming, and Continuous Quality Improvement (CQI) to provide technical consulting and subject matter expertise supporting the County’s development and implementation of its Family First Prevention Services Program. The selected Contractor will serve as a technical advisor to the County by providing strategic consultation, policy and operational guidance, fiscal expertise, workforce planning recommendations, facilitation, and technical assistance necessary to support the County in designing and implementing a sustainable FFPSA Prevention Program that complies with applicable federal and State requirements. The Contractor will work collaboratively with County leadership, child welfare program staff, fiscal staff, and community partners to provide technical guidance, develop implementation recommendations, and assist the County in making informed policy and operational decisions. The County will retain responsibility for all policy decisions, operational implementation, eligibility determinations, and ongoing administration of the FFPSA Prevention Program. The Contractor will not assume operational responsibility for County programs, perform child welfare case management functions, or make eligibility determinations on behalf of the County. The County seeks a consultant with extensive knowledge of California child welfare systems and FFPSA requirements who can provide practical guidance, develop implementation tools and resources, identify regulatory and operational considerations, and support integration of Title IV-E Prevention requirements into the County’s existing child welfare continuum. A successful result looks like a fully integrated, state-compliant Title IV-E and Community Pathway network that routes families to evidence-based programs (EBPs) without requiring Child Protective Services (CPS) involvement. The selected contractor will successfully establish auditable Title IV-E candidacy determination tools, build a braided fiscal model to maximize federal revenue alongside Medi-Cal (CalAIM), and ensure complete documentation and data-link readiness prior to the upcoming CWS-CARES platform local go-live deployment. The County intends to award one agreement for an initial term of two (2) years, tentatively beginning in September 2026.

opportunities.title: Salesforce Test Automation
opportunities.description: San Mateo County is a dynamic and diverse county on the San Francisco Peninsula, spanning approximately 455 square miles between the Pacific Ocean and San Francisco Bay and serving nearly 800,000 residents across 20 incorporated cities and communities that range from dense urban centers to suburban neighborhoods and rural coastal areas. Established in April 1856, San Mateo County has grown into a nationally recognized hub of innovation and technology at the heart of Silicon Valley. The County boasts a thriving economy supported by industries such as bioscience, internet commerce, computer software, green technology, hospitality, financial management, health care, education, and transportation. What truly defines San Mateo County is its cultural, geographic, and economic diversity. The County is deeply committed to preserving its natural assets, nearly three-quarters of its land is open space, and agriculture continues to contribute to its economy and culture. San Mateo County provides essential services that protect and enhance the health, safety, welfare, and quality of life of all people, while embracing a tradition of public service, inclusion, and forward-thinking approaches to meeting community needs. The County has recently implemented a new Assessor Property Assessment System (APAS) to manage the assessment and valuation of properties with San Mateo County. As with any new system, changes and fixes are required as gaps and defects are identified through production usage. As these changes are deployed with new code, the staff within the Assessor Division of the Assessor-County Clerk-Recorder and Elections (ACRE) Department are currently performing highly complex UAT testing of highly detail multistep processes. Because the testing requires a high level of knowledge and expertise in the subject area, only a limited dedicated staff can perform such tests. And because the various modules are so intertwined with each other, a more thorough level of regression testing is also required. However, these staff also have other duties including operational support which limit available time to perform the testing. Thus, the Department is seeking an automated Salesforce testing solution which can increase their available bandwidth or possibly even offload the testing process to other less experienced staff.

opportunities.description: The County of Sacramento (County) owns and/or operates four airports in Sacramento County, including Sacramento International Airport (SMF or Airport), Mather Airport (MHR), Sacramento Executive Airport (SAC), and Franklin Field (F72) through the Department of Airports (SCDA or Department). The data must support consistent asset hierarchies, condition scoring, and lifecycle modeling. The data must also align with SCDA’s existing ProDIGIQ AMS QR-code/barcode generation and asset identification standards, enabling scan-to-asset linkage for inspections, preventive maintenance, and work order history.

opportunities.title: Probation Department Annual Training Curriculum Services
opportunities.description: The San Mateo County Probation Department (“Department”) employs approximately 220-250 staff in three (3) locations: Redwood City, San Mateo, and South San Francisco. Probation personnel encompass a wide variety of diverse professionals in both Sworn and Non-Sworn capacities. The Department is responsible for the supervision of approximately 2,500 adult and juvenile probationers. Probation represents the link between the application of appropriate consequences for illegal and delinquent behavior and the establishment of offenders transitioning to productive, law-abiding lives. This specialized criminal justice role of probation is a successful and cost-effective balance of both enforcement and treatment. Deputy Probation Officers (DPOs) are responsible for monitoring probationers in the community by enforcing court-ordered restrictions and providing access to rehabilitation programs, as well as promoting victim safety and restoration. The Department's Professional Standards Unit coordinates and conducts mandated training for sworn officers, as well as administrative professionals. The Department is seeking qualified vendors to provide annual, standards-compliant training services for approximately 220-250 S worn and Non-Sworn probation staff across adult, juvenile and institutions, and administrative divisions. The Department’s mission includes ensuring public safety, staff readiness, legal compliance, and evidence-based supervision practices. Annual training is mandated by regulatory bodies, including the Board of State and Community Corrections (BSCC), California Commission on Peace Officer Standards and Training (POST), and California Code of Regulations Title 15. The goal is to standardize skills sets and ensure high-level professional growth across the 2027 to 2030 training calendar year. Subject to compliance with all terms and conditions, the timeline for the term of this Agreement shall be up to three (3) years, with a commencing start date of July 1, 2027, including one (1) option to extend the term for an additional period not to exceed two (2) years. The Department requires a comprehensive, scalable, and compliant training program that: Ensures all staff meet annual certification requirements Enhances officer safety and field readiness Maintains legal and procedural compliance Incorporates modern training methodologies The Department reserves the right to award multiple contracts by training discipline, or award a single prime contractor with subcontractors.

Eligible participants will be diverted from the criminal justice system into immediate interim housing with wraparound services such as case management, behavioral health therapy, substance use counseling, housing navigation and job training. The program aims to reduce recidivism, homelessness, and improve public health and safety in Pasadena.

Providers must be Board-Certified Child and Adolescent Psychiatrist, or board-eligible in child and adolescent psychiatry and actively pursuing board certification resulting in board-certification within 1 year of eligibility. Providers may contract individually or through a qualifying medical group or organization. All providers must adhere to applicable California laws, regulations, and professional standards of care. Contractors are required to comply with all regulatory requirements, facility policies and procedures, and expectations for coordination with YDF leadership and oversight entities. Applicants must meet all stated Minimum Qualifications (MQs) to be eligible for contract consideration with DHS. Contracts may be executed on a rolling basis based on County need and must be fully executed before the delivery of services or submission of invoices. Approval through this Open Enrollment does not guarantee referral volume or funding. County funding is limited to reimbursement for approved direct service costs only.
